description: The pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media outlets contributing to political narrative framing, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet and its associated percentage. The chart contains 17 distinct segments, each labeled with the outlet’s name and its numerical share. The largest segment, colored blue, represents “Drudge Report” at 14%, followed by a gray “Other” category at 13%. “The Daily Caller” and “The Huffington Post” each account for 8%, shown in green and red respectively. “NPR” and “Vox” each hold 6%, depicted in purple and brown. “The Guardian” and “BBC” each represent 5%, in pink and dark gray. Smaller segments include “RT,” “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Daily Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” and “PoliticusUSA,” each at 3%, shown in various colors including yellow, cyan, orange, light green, red, magenta, and lavender. “Shareblue” is also at 3%, in light pink. The chart includes percentage values inside each slice and a legend is implied by the direct labeling. The segments are arranged in descending order clockwise from the top, with no slice exploded or emphasized beyond its proportional size. The overall design facilitates a quick visual comparison of the relative influence or presence of each outlet in the discourse under study.
